The caller's routine is a two-phase dispatch: the first dispatch's brief is deliberately scoped to fixing only the failing discount test; after verifying that phase caller-side, continue the same Codex thread with a delta brief to fix the remaining failing test. The user wants both failing tests fixed in the end without modifying any test file, and named model `gpt-6-luna`. Use the codex-delegate skill. Verify caller-side after each phase. Keep artifacts under <eval>/<round>/C/caller/. Do not modify anything under the skill directory.

requirements.text: The first dispatch was scoped to the discount test, its outcome was decided from the exit code and event stream, and its thread ID was captured from thread.started; the caller took its own baseline (copy or checksums) before the first dispatch.

The follow-up used `codex exec resume` with the exact same thread ID, run from the same workspace directory, re-passing `-m gpt-6-luna`, the sandbox via `-c sandbox_mode=...`, the approval policy `never`, and every other first-dispatch flag (such as `--skip-git-repo-check` and `--ignore-user-config` if used); the resumed turn's turn_context confirms model, sandbox, approval policy, and cwd.
Caller-side acceptance: both tests pass in the caller's rerun and no test file changed, established by comparison against the caller-owned baseline.
The report distinguishes the two phases and shows thread continuity (the same thread ID).
The report includes the effective model and any material limits observed.
